parseAudit.decision: The old 3-parse-error inventory is retained as historical evidence but does not define the canonical correctness cohort. The later canonical audit already records 6 parse errors plus 13 mixed-board exclusions and exactly 8,650 canonical cases.

correctnessPredicate.rule: For a feasible input, correctness means a fresh plan that is geometrically/industrially valid and covers exactly the demanded piece multiset. A demanded piece that cannot fit the usable board in any allowed orientation makes the input expected-infeasible rather than an optimizer regression.
correctnessPredicate.referencePanelsRole: reference_panels / delta is a quality comparison versus Lepton and is reported, but it is not the historical correctness acceptance gate.
evidence: benchmark_project_v10.csv records estado and delta independently.
10 rows are estado=OK with delta>0, so using more boards than Lepton was still accepted as correct.
33 rows are estado=ERROR with delta<=0, so non-worse board count did not make an invalid plan correct.
The 93 ERROR rows split into 33 exact-demand/multiset failures and 60 physically infeasible inputs; 450 SKIP rows are format-scope exclusions.

infeasibleClassification.method: Derive from the exact 8,650 physical XML cohort after parsing with the current canonical parser: a piece is impossible when neither its direct orientation nor any orientation allowed by rotation constraints fits the usable panel.
infeasibleClassification.execution: Expected-infeasible cases count toward correctness classification coverage but are not sent to optimizeProject and are excluded from fullPlanHash determinism denominators.

deterministicBudgets.rule: Do not run formal determinism certification with absent, guessed, smoke-test, or CI-convenience budgets. Calibrate from aggregate per-order Step 0 work on the production-representative exact cohort. Watchdog hits must be zero during formal certification.

calibrationProtocol.inputSource: physical resto XML parsed through the current src/lib/optimizer/canonical-xml.ts runtime
calibrationProtocol.initialOrder: cheap-to-expensive proxy; historical hotspot engineMs when known, then piece count; known extreme-tail orders forced last
calibrationProtocol.beamRule: Calibrate maxExpansionesBeam from aggregate per-order Beam work, not by converting the historical presupuestoBeamMs=1500 per invocation into expansions.
calibrationProtocol.aggregateBudgetDecision: Do not add a new aggregate request stop condition inside Kernel V1 freeze. That changes search semantics and requires a new Kernel V1 candidate plus all gates.
calibrationProtocol.promotionRequirement: Version explicit positive integer production values with calibration evidence before formal correctness/determinism certification.

ordering.calibration: historical timing where available, then piece-count proxy; known extreme tail last
ordering.correctness: calibration measured wallMs ascending when available

partialCoverage: correctness: classified cases / 8650, including expected-infeasible classifications
determinism-repeat: repeated feasible plan cases / feasible cases
determinism-repeat timing mass: sum of baseline correctness wallMs for repeated feasible cases / total feasible correctness wallMs
calibration: completed feasible cases plus separately scoped historical-hotspot timing-mass coverage

blockingReasons: Production deterministic budgets/watchdogs are not calibrated and versioned.
